examples.input: Our AWS bill is $45,000/month. Biggest items: EC2 ($18,000), RDS ($8,000), data transfer ($6,000), S3 ($4,000), ECS/Fargate ($5,000), everything else ($4,000). We're a 20-person startup with staging and production environments. No Reserved Instances or Savings Plans.

quick_wins.action: Purchase Compute Savings Plan (1-year, no upfront) for baseline EC2+Fargate usage
quick_wins.implementation: Analyze last 30 days of compute usage in Cost Explorer → Savings Plans recommendations. Cover 70-80% of baseline with 1-year no-upfront plan. This alone saves 24-30% on compute.

quick_wins.action: Delete unused EBS volumes and old snapshots
quick_wins.implementation: aws ec2 describe-volumes --filters Name=status,Values=available | List and review each. Delete volumes unused for >30 days.

quick_wins.action: Shut down staging environment outside business hours (7pm-7am + weekends)
quick_wins.implementation: Use AWS Instance Scheduler or a simple Lambda + EventBridge rule to stop/start staging EC2, RDS, and ECS services. Saves ~65% of staging compute costs.

medium_effort.action: Right-size EC2 instances based on actual CPU/memory utilization
medium_effort.implementation: Enable AWS Compute Optimizer. Review recommendations for each instance. Typical finding: teams use m5.xlarge when m5.large would suffice. Test in staging first.

medium_effort.action: Implement S3 Intelligent-Tiering and lifecycle policies
medium_effort.implementation: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering for all buckets. Add lifecycle rules: transition to IA after 30 days, Glacier after 90 days for logs and backups. Expected 60-70% reduction in S3 costs.

strategic_initiatives.action: Optimize data transfer architecture with VPC endpoints and CloudFront
strategic_initiatives.implementation: 1. Add VPC endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB (free, eliminates NAT Gateway data processing fees). 2. Put CloudFront in front of API for cacheable responses. 3. Review cross-AZ traffic patterns.

examples.input: We're running 15 GPU instances (p3.2xlarge) on AWS for ML training jobs. They run 24/7 but actual training only happens about 40 hours per week. Monthly GPU cost is around $70,000.

current_spend.utilization: 24% (40 hours actual use out of 168 hours/week)
current_spend.waste: 76% of GPU spend is idle time

quick_wins.action: Stop GPU instances when not training (implement on-demand scheduling)
quick_wins.implementation: Use AWS Step Functions or a simple scheduler to start instances when training jobs are queued and stop them when complete. With 40hr/week usage, you only pay for 24% of the current cost. Even with 15 minutes of startup overhead per job, savings are massive.

quick_wins.action: Use Spot Instances for fault-tolerant training jobs
quick_wins.implementation: p3.2xlarge spot pricing is typically 60-70% off on-demand. Implement checkpointing every 30 minutes so interrupted training can resume. Use spot fleet with diversified instance types (p3.2xlarge, g5.2xlarge) for better availability.

examples.input: Can you review our GCP project spending? We use GKE, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and Pub/Sub. Monthly bill is $22,000 and growing 15% month over month. We're a Series A startup with 50,000 users.

output.analysis_approach: At 15% MoM growth, aggressive cost cutting is less important than unit economics optimization. Focus on ensuring cost scales sub-linearly with users — cost per user should decrease, not increase.

quick_wins.action: Enable GKE cluster autoscaler and right-size node pools
quick_wins.implementation: 1. Enable cluster autoscaler with min 2, max 10 nodes. 2. Switch to e2 machine types (20% cheaper than n1). 3. Use node auto-provisioning to match workload shapes. 4. Set resource requests/limits on all pods to enable efficient bin-packing.

quick_wins.action: Optimize BigQuery with partitioning and query cost controls
quick_wins.implementation: 1. Partition tables by date. 2. Require partition filters on large tables. 3. Set per-user query cost quotas. 4. Convert frequently-run queries to materialized views. 5. Consider switching heavy analytics tables to BigQuery BI Engine.

output.strategic_note: At Series A with 50K users growing 15% MoM, your priority should be: (1) track cost-per-user trend monthly, (2) ensure committed use discounts cover baseline, (3) optimize the highest-growth cost categories. Don't over-invest engineering time in saving $200/month — focus on the items that will matter at 500K users.
